Channel Islands by Motorcycle: A Unique British Adventure

The Channel Islands sit just off the French coast but are British Crown Dependencies with their own character. Jersey and Guernsey offer a unique motorcycling experience — compact islands with dramatic coastal roads, WWII bunkers, French-influenced culture, and a relaxed pace of life. It's like touring a different country without leaving the UK.

Jersey Routes

Jersey is the larger island at 9 miles by 5 miles, with about 350 miles of roads. The speed limit is 40mph (lower in green lanes), so this is about leisurely exploration rather than fast riding.

The north coast road from St Helier to Greve de Lecq is Jersey's finest ride. Dramatic cliffs, hidden bays, and views across to France create a coastal experience unlike anything on the British mainland. The roads wind through the headlands with frequent viewpoints.

The Green Lanes are Jersey's network of priority lanes where the speed limit is 15mph. These connect farms, churches, and hidden corners of the island. On a motorcycle, they're charming — like riding through a living museum of rural life.

Guernsey Routes

Guernsey is smaller than Jersey but arguably more characterful. The island's rugged south coast contrasts with the gentle north, and the interior is a maze of narrow lanes. The coast road from St Peter Port south to Pleinmont offers spectacular cliff-top riding. Fort Grey (the Cup and Saucer) and the German fortifications are worth stopping for.

The Island-Hopping Circuit

With Condor Ferries connecting Jersey, Guernsey, and the UK mainland, you can create a multi-day island-hopping tour. Ferry from Poole to Guernsey, explore for two days, ferry to Jersey for two more days, then return to Poole. Allow 5-6 days total for a relaxed circuit.

The Channel Islands feel like a motorcycle-friendly version of France — the food is better, the weather is warmer, and the roads are emptier than the British mainland.

Practical Information

  • Ferries: Condor Ferries from Poole (3 hours high-speed) or Portsmouth. Book motorcycle spaces well in advance for summer
  • Fuel: Cheaper than the UK mainland — fill up on the islands
  • Speed limits: 40mph max on Jersey, 35mph on Guernsey. Green lanes 15mph
  • Currency: Sterling accepted everywhere, though islands issue their own notes
  • Riding side: Left-hand drive, same as the UK mainland

What to See

The Channel Islands are steeped in WWII history — they were the only British territory occupied by Nazi Germany. The underground hospital in Jersey and the German fortifications across both islands are fascinating and sobering. Beyond the war history, enjoy the beaches, seafood restaurants, and the unique Anglo-Norman culture that makes these islands special.
keyTakeaways: Jersey and Guernsey are British Crown Dependencies off the French coast with their own character and low speed limits.
Jersey is 9 miles by 5 with about 350 miles of roads and a 40mph maximum limit; Guernsey's max is 35mph.
Jersey's Green Lanes are priority lanes with a 15mph limit, ideal for leisurely exploration.
Condor Ferries link Jersey, Guernsey and the mainland, allowing a 5 to 6 day island-hopping circuit from Poole.
The islands were the only British territory occupied in WWII, so bunkers and fortifications are everywhere.

faq.q: What are the speed limits on the Channel Islands?
faq.a: Jersey has a 40mph maximum, dropping to 15mph on its network of priority Green Lanes, while Guernsey's maximum is 35mph. This is about leisurely exploration rather than fast riding, so relax the pace and enjoy the coastal scenery, hidden bays and French-influenced culture.

faq.q: How do I get there with a motorcycle?
faq.a: Condor Ferries connect the islands with the UK mainland, running from Poole in about three hours on the high-speed service, or from Portsmouth. Book motorcycle spaces well in advance for summer. Fuel is cheaper than on the mainland, so fill up once you arrive on the islands.

faq.q: Can I visit both islands in one trip?
faq.a: Yes. With Condor Ferries connecting Jersey, Guernsey and the mainland, you can build a multi-day island-hopping tour. Ferry from Poole to Guernsey, explore for two days, ferry to Jersey for two more, then return to Poole. Allow five to six days total for a relaxed circuit.

Jersey's north coast road from St Helier to Greve de Lecq has dramatic cliffs and views to France, while Guernsey's south coast from St Peter Port to Pleinmont offers spectacular cliff-top riding. Both islands are steeped in WWII history, with German fortifications and underground sites well worth a stop.
